number.why: The reported primary-composite HR is 0.69 with 95% CI 0.57–0.83 for colchicine versus placebo, with median follow-up of 28.6 months. Agreement concerns the reported number; the served intention-to-treat population is not explicitly established, as the ruling correctly acknowledges.

quotes.span: The primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, spontaneous (nonprocedural) myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or ischemia-driven coronary revascularization.

A primary end-point event occurred in 187 patients (6.8%) in the colchicine group and in 264 patients (9.6%) in the placebo group (incidence, 2.5 vs. 3.6 events per 100 person-years; hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.83; P<0.001).
The median duration of follow-up was 28.6 months.
A total of 5522 patients underwent randomization; 2762 were assigned to the colchicine group and 2760 to the placebo group.

entry.why: The sources establish chronic coronary disease and a randomized, double-blind comparison of low-dose colchicine with placebo. Neither source explicitly establishes adult ages or adult-only eligibility. Therefore the full entry population in the question is only partly established.

quotes.span: In a randomized, controlled, double-blind trial, we assigned patients with chronic coronary disease to receive 0.5 mg of colchicine once daily or matching placebo.
In a randomized, controlled, double-blind trial, we assigned patients with chronic coronary disease to receive 0.5 mg of colchicine once daily or matching placebo.

missed: The ruling acknowledges that adult age criteria are unstated but does not carry that limitation into its ESTABLISHED entry ruling. The numerical match also does not establish the served intention-to-treat label; that limitation was already identified correctly.
